title: Timeline: Fifteen years of Egypt-Ethiopia dam dispute – BBC Monitoring
text:
Timeline: Fifteen years of Egypt-Ethiopia dam dispute – BBC Monitoring

12 September 2025

13:10 GMT

# Timeline: Fifteen years of Egypt-Ethiopia dam dispute

 Ethiopia officially launched its controversial dam on 9 September 

Ethiopia officially launched its Nile megadam, the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD), on 9 September in a ceremony attended by Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed and senior government officials.

Addis Ababa announced the completion of the GERD's construction two months before the inauguration in July.

The inauguration of the controversial dam is expected to open a new chapter of the conflict between Ethiopia on one hand and Egypt and Sudan on the other. 

The GERD has been a source of contention between Egypt, Sudan and Ethiopia since Addis Ababa announced it would start building the mega dam upstream on the River Nile in 2011 with a $4bn budget. The Blue Nile dam is regarded as Africa's largest hydroelectric power plant.

The three countries have engaged in protracted talks for over 14 years to reach an agreement over the GERD, to no avail. Ethiopia, however, has unilaterally completed all the phases of filling up the dam, as this has always given rise to major concern in downstream Egypt and Sudan. 

Over the years, Cairo and Khartoum have come to develop closer ties, especially military cooperation, as they try to coordinate moves to face Ethiopia's uncompromising stances. Egypt has always reiterated that it will defend its water rights by all means, and that its Nile water share is "an existential matter".

The outbreak of rebellion in Sudan in 2023, earlier rebellions in some Ethiopian regions, as well as a border dispute between Ethiopia and Sudan in late 2020, constituted a significant game changer in their positions in the dam talks. Sudan has at times shifted to rapprochement with Ethiopia, but also at other times from a position that has been seen by some as ambiguous to joining forces with Cairo against Addis Ababa.

Ethiopia's Benishangul-Gumuz Region, which is home for the controversial dam on the Blue Nile, has been blighted by armed attacks in recent years. Relations with Ethiopia's neighbours, especially Somalia and Eritrea, are believed to have been used, especially by Egypt, as a card in the GERD dispute.

Below is a timeline of key developments related to the GERD row:

## 2011

March: The Ethiopian government announces its ambitious plan to build a multi-billion-dollar dam, set to be Africa's largest hydroelectric power station.

April: Dam construction begins.

May: Egypt, Sudan and Ethiopia agree on a tripartite technical committee to study the impact of the dam.

September: Ethiopia says the dam will not affect Egypt's Nile water quota. The Egyptian prime minister says the dam could be beneficial to both sides, during the Ethiopian prime minister's visit to Cairo.

## 2012

May: The International Panel of Experts (IPoE) composed of the tripartite committee and four foreign experts starts its work to assess the impact of the dam.

October: IPoE pays its first visit to the dam's construction site. The panel visited the site four times in the year.

## 2013

May: Ethiopia diverts the course of the Blue Nile.

June: IPoE submits its final report. Ethiopia and Egypt differ in their interpretation of the report. Egyptian President Mohammed Morsi sharpens his tone against dam on different occasions and holds a televised meeting with political powers, where the use of force against Ethiopia is suggested. Ethiopia requests formal clarification about these remarks and escalates tone on dam. Egypt threatens to resort to the International Court of Justice. The two countries later agree to launch political, technical tracks to implement IPoE recommendations.

September: Egyptian and Ethiopian foreign ministers meet in New York on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly and agree to resume talks over the dam.

November: Egyptian, Sudanese and Ethiopian water ministers meet in Khartoum to discuss IPoE recommendations; no agreement reached.

December: Egyptian, Sudanese and Ethiopian water ministers hold a second meeting in Khartoum. They fail to agree on the composition of the panel to provide technical expertise on IPoE recommendations.

## 2014

January: Egyptian, Sudanese and Ethiopian water ministers hold a third meeting in Khartoum. They decide to suspend meetings indefinitely after failing to resolve pending issues.

February: Egypt's water minister holds talks with his Ethiopian counterpart in Addis Ababa; no progress made.

March: Egypt's foreign ministry says it is intensifying efforts to convince the international community of Egypt's position regarding the dam.

April: Ethiopia asks Egypt to stop campaigning against the dam. Ethiopia urges Egypt to return to tripartite dialogue.

June: Egyptian President Abdul Fattah al-Sisi and Ethiopian Prime Minister Hailemariam Desalegn meet on the sidelines of the African summit in Malabo, Equatorial Guinea. They agree on the immediate resumption of the activities of the tripartite committee.

August: Egyptian, Sudanese and Ethiopian water ministers resume their meetings in Khartoum. They agree to form a committee of experts from the three countries, under the supervision of an international consultancy firm, to conduct studies on the impact of the dam as recommended by the IPoE.

September: The water ministers of Egypt and Sudan visit the dam. The first meeting of the Tripartite National Committee (TNC) takes place in Addis Ababa.

October: TNC meets in Cairo to choose an international consultancy firm to conduct further studies on the dam.

## 2015

January: Egypt rejects the dam's height and storage capacity of 74 billion cubic metres.

March: Third TNC meeting held in Khartoum. The three countries sign a Declaration of Principles on the dam. The Egyptian president delivers a speech at the Ethiopian parliament.

April: TNC meets in Addis Ababa and selects two European advisory offices to conduct technical studies on the dam.

July: New round of TNC meetings kicks off in Cairo to review offers by two European advisory offices. The three countries agree on the scope and mechanism of the work of the advisory offices during a TNC meeting in Khartoum.

November: TNC meets in Cairo, where disagreements between the two European advisory offices are discussed. Egypt requests a meeting of the three countries' ministers of foreign affairs and irrigation to develop a technical roadmap.

December: TNC meets in Sudan. The Khartoum Document signed, setting a one-year deadline for completing the dam studies and selecting another European advisory office after one of them withdraws.

## 2016

January: The Egyptian president and Ethiopian prime minister meet in Addis Ababa and affirm their commitment to the Khartoum Document and understanding of each other's rights.

February: TNC holds a meeting in Khartoum and examines a joint technical proposal submitted by the two French advisory firms assigned to probe the effects of the dam on Sudan and Egypt.

September: TNC signs a contract with the French consulting company, BRLi, to commence the two IPoE-recommended studies on the GERD.

## 2017

February: Two French advisory firms submit their preliminary report on the dam. Egypt accepts it while Ethiopia and Sudan reject it.

April: Egyptian president meets Ethiopian foreign minister in Cairo and stresses the need to reach an agreement on filling the dam in accordance with the declaration of principles that was signed in Khartoum.

October: TNC holds a meeting to discuss differences over the studies submitted by two French consultancy firms.

November: TNC holds meeting in Cairo; no progress made. The Ethiopian foreign ministry accuses Egypt of creating problems.

December: Egypt's foreign minister expresses great concern over dam talks as he flies to Addis Ababa for talks with his Ethiopian counterpart.

## 2018

January: The Egyptian president expresses concern over the stalemate in the talks; renews proposal to involve the World Bank. Ethiopia rejects Egypt's proposal. Egypt, Sudan and Ethiopia agree to form an annual trilateral summit , to establish a joint infrastructure fund and form a committee of the three countries' foreign ministers and directors of intelligence and security services to solve all sticking points within a month.

April: The foreign ministers, irrigation ministers and heads of intelligence of Sudan, Ethiopia and Egypt meet in Khartoum. The meeting ends with "no specific results".

May: The foreign and irrigation ministers as well as the intelligence chiefs of Egypt, Sudan and Ethiopia meet in Addis Ababa. Egypt says the meeting was "successful".

June: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed arrives in Cairo on his first visit since assuming office. He vows in Arabic "not to harm water in Egypt", a vow jokingly dictated by the Egyptian president during a press conference in Cairo.

September: Egypt refuses to sign an agreement on filling the dam.

November: Egyptian and Ethiopian prime ministers meet on the sidelines of an African Union summit in Addis Ababa and agree to accelerate the dam talks.

## 2019

April: Egypt says Ethiopia dam talks on pause amid protests in Sudan.

July: The Egyptian president meets the Ethiopian foreign minister in Cairo. They agree to resume trilateral talks on the dam.

September: The Egyptian foreign minister says his country is not satisfied with prolonged negotiations. Ethiopia rejects the Egyptian proposal on filling the dam. The Egyptian president warns Ethiopia against bringing the dam into operation.

October: The White House issues a statement for the first time on the Ethiopian dam talks. Egypt announces a deadlock in dam negotiations with Ethiopia and asks for the mediation of another party. Egypt urges the US to play a more active role in the talks. Ethiopia criticises Egypt's call. The Ethiopian prime minister tells parliament that no force can stop his country from building dams. Egypt criticises his statements and accepts a US invitation to a meeting on the dam in Washington. The Egyptian and Ethiopian leaders meet in Sochi on the sidelines of Russia-Africa summit and agree to immediately resume TNC meetings.

November: US-sponsored talks start. The ministers of foreign affairs and water of Egypt, Ethiopia and Sudan meet in Washington, followed by a meeting between the water ministers in Addis Ababa with the presence of US and World Bank representatives. Upbeat tone about talks in Ethiopia and Egypt.

December: Three more meetings take place in Cairo, Washington and Khartoum in the presence of US and World Bank representatives. Ethiopian water minister dubs talks "successful" and says that Egypt dropped its proposal on filling the dam. Egypt denies this.

## 2020

January: The ministers of foreign affairs and water of Egypt, Sudan and Ethiopia meet twice in Washington, while the ministers of water meet once in Addis Ababa. The legal and technical working groups of the three countries meet in Khartoum. Talks are extended for another month after initially being scheduled to end mid-January. Conflicting reports from Egypt and Ethiopia about reaching an agreement.

February: Both the legal and technical working groups and the ministers of foreign affairs and water hold meetings in Washington. Ethiopia abstains from attending the final meetings in Washington on 27-28 February. Egypt attends and signs the US-mediated agreement on the filling and operation of the dam.

March: Egypt uses sharp rhetoric against Ethiopia after the latter backtracks on signing a US-mediated deal. Top Ethiopian military officers say army is ready to defend the dam. Ethiopian foreign minister accuses the US of being biased in its mediation of the dam talks. Egypt's foreign minister goes on an Arab tour to rally support for the country's position. Ethiopia rejects Arab League resolution on GERD over showing support for Egypt.
